notes.text: The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 30% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the 6th-lowest in the league (a typical team: 38%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.

Igor Chernyshov is on injured reserve (upper-body injury) and has missed the last 17 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Ivar Stenberg has taken his spot beside Will Smith and Macklin Celebrini. That line has had 61% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 69:09 together, about what it had with Chernyshov (60%).
Kiefer Sherwood is on injured reserve and has missed the last 5 games.

Jacob Trouba is out (lower body injury) and has missed the last 3 games. He is a top-pair defenseman. Nolan Allan has taken his spot beside Sam Dickinson. That pair has had 66% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 38:18 together, up from 43% with Trouba.
Nathan MacKinnon is out (lower-body injury) and has missed the last 5 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters.
Martin Nečas is out and missed their last game. He is a top-six forward.
Mike Reilly was added to the roster on Nov 16 and has played beside Brent Burns.
Zachary L'Heureux is no longer killing penalties: 3% of the team’s shorthanded time in 3 games, down from 36% with his old team last season.

story.head: A long night for Alex Nedeljkovic
paras: The Avalanche have won three straight, and the Sharks (12-14-2) beat Vegas 4-1 last night. Going in, the Sharks are third in the Pacific (tied for 19th in the NHL) and the Avalanche second in the Central (tied for seventh).

The Sharks are one of the league’s most physical teams (3rd), ice the puck a lot (32nd) and have a leaky penalty kill (31st). San Jose has scored 2.57 goals a game, the second fewest in the league. On the other side, the Avalanche do a lot of their shooting from distance (most). They also throw more pucks at the net than almost anyone (2nd), so the Avs are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Sharks. Colorado has scored 3.96 goals a game, the second most in the league. Both teams like to play fast, especially the Avalanche (1st), so expect an open game.

Macklin Celebrini (11 G / 22 A / 33 P in 26 GP) is carrying the Sharks’ offense. For the Avalanche, Cale Makar (5 G / 22 A / 27 P in 21 GP) leads the way in scoring, with a point in six straight games against San Jose. Artturi Lehkonen (17 G / 8 A / 25 P in 25 GP) has a team-high 17 goals, tied for fifth in the NHL.
Alex Nedeljkovic (5-4-1 / .888 SV% in 10 GS) will likely start for San Jose, and Scott Wedgewood (2-3-2 / .882 SV% in 7 GS) for Colorado.

At home, Jared Bednar likes to send Makar, Kelly and O'Connor out against opponents’ fourth lines, so watch for them against Goodrow, Ostapchuk and Graf. Elsewhere, the Avalanche usually control more of the chances than the Sharks do.

items.text: The Sharks are newly without Jacob Trouba, and have been without Igor Chernyshov and Kiefer Sherwood for several games.

The Avalanche are newly without Martin Nečas, and have been without Nathan MacKinnon since Nov 12. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, only the Mammoth are missing more right now.
With Nathan MacKinnon out, Parker Kelly took eight faceoffs in the Avalanche’s last game. He had been taking about two a game.
Artturi Lehkonen has 17 goals on chances worth about 9.8 goals, well above what his finishing usually turns chances into. Runs like that tend to cool off.
